threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still don’t know the secret cafe behind the barbershop on Kingsland Road. Trust me, the espresso’s a game-changer.
Last night on the 59, a lad proposed to his girlfriend at Stockwell. The whole bus cheered, but she just sat there, completely blank-faced.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw an old man feeding pigeons with a slice of pizza in the middle of a protest—no one batted an eye. That's when I knew I belonged.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a techno party inside a former public toilet—complete with graffiti and a proper bar. The spirit of Berlin is truly underground.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they casually step over the dog that's taken a nap on the Muni tracks like it's just a part of their morning commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 after the BART chaos. A guy started rapping about the delays, everyone chuckled. Only in SF do we turn transit misery into a live show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the trendy bars, but locals know it's the neighborhood's unassuming bakeries that keep the heart beating.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones wandering around with a map in hand, still trying to figure out how to navigate the winding streets of Gràcia without GPS.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look bewildered when the bus driver shouts 'Next stop, get off!' like it’s a personal attack.
Caught a glimpse of a sleeping man on the 35 last night, cradling a half-eaten pepperoni pizza like it was a baby. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found out my favorite bakery was open at 6 AM, just as a group of night owls wrapped up their evening. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24/7 Döner place where the line is always longer than at the club around the corner. Late-night cravings sorted!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals will know to avoid BART on rainy days; they don't just bring umbrellas, they bring snacks for the inevitable delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni stuck in the Civic Center loop yesterday. A dog on the tracks and a saxophonist jamming nearby made for an oddly charming chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real gem is the small artists' ateliers tucked away in corners, each with a story to tell.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered look at the metro ticket machines—totally lost in translation with the options.
